tools.name: status
tools.description: Whether tunnel is up and how it is set right now: version, the three directories, how many rules and logged requests it holds, the session in hand, whether recording is on, the proxy address a device points at, the CA fingerprint, and what every session on disk holds. Make this the first call.

tools.name: guide
tools.description: tunnel's AGENTS.md, the copy this version ships: the handler(ctx) API a script rule is written against, how a request key is matched, how replay picks a recording, and the steps of a test run. Read it before writing rules. Needs no running server.

tools.name: list_mocks
tools.description: Every rule as it stands, whole, in the shape apply_scenario takes back — so this is also how a set of rules is exported. A key narrows it to one.

key.description: a rule key as list_mocks reports it, METHOD:/path or METHOD:host/path

tools.name: set_mock
tools.description: Configure what one endpoint answers; only the fields passed change. Give exactly one source — json_response, json_file, script, script_file, target or replay — and it settles the mode. Everything else shapes whatever that mode answers.

path.description: a path (/api/feed), or a host and path (api.example.com/api/feed); * is a wildcard in either

json_response.description: the JSON body to answer with; sets mode json

json_file.description: a file holding that JSON, read here and sent inline; sets mode json

script.description: JavaScript or TypeScript defining handler(ctx), run per request; sets mode script. The guide tool has the ctx API

script_file.description: a file holding that script, read here and sent inline; sets mode script

target.description: pass through to this base URL or full URL instead of the request's own origin; sets mode passthrough

replay.description: answer from the recordings instead of the real server; sets mode replay

mode.description: set the mode outright; wins over the one a source implies

status_code.description: the status code to answer with

delay.description: hold the answer back this many seconds

headers.description: response headers; these replace the rule's headers rather than adding to them

content_type.description: the content type of the response, folded into headers

merge.description: deep merged into the JSON that comes back, in passthrough and replay

fault.description: answer wrongly on purpose: hang holds the request for fault_seconds then 504, garbage does not parse as the JSON it claims, close drops the connection unanswered

fault_seconds.description: how long a hang fault holds the request

strategy.description: which recording replay picks: the one whose query matches, the next in order, or the newest

session.description: pin this rule to one recorded session; empty follows the current one

enabled.description: false parks the rule without deleting it

tools.name: delete_mock
tools.description: Delete one rule. The request log is left alone.

key.description: a rule key as list_mocks reports it, METHOD:/path or METHOD:host/path

tools.name: apply_scenario
tools.description: Apply a set of rules in one call, all of them or none of them: a scenario file on disk, or the scenario itself. Give exactly one of the two.

file.description: a scenario file; its script_file and json_file are resolved beside it and sent inline

scenario.description: the scenario itself, as {"mocks": [...]} with an optional "config"

replace.description: clear the rules configured now first

tools.name: list_requests
tools.description: What the client actually called: one row per endpoint with counts, or one row per request with each. unmatched answers 'what have I not mocked yet', since answers 'what arrived after that seq'.

each.description: one row per request instead of the aggregate

key.description: only this rule key; wildcards allowed

host.description: only this host; * is a wildcard

since.description: only what arrived after this seq

encrypted.description: only tunnels that were not decrypted

q.description: keyword: host, path, query, status, rule

q_body.description: let the keyword search the bodies too

tools.name: get_request
tools.description: One call in full: headers and bodies, request and response. Header values that carry a session come back [REDACTED] unless raw is set.

seq.description: the seq from list_requests with each

tools.name: wait_for_request
tools.description: Block until the client has made this call, instead of sleeping and hoping. Running out of time is not an error: the answer says timed_out and which seqs were seen.

path.description: a path (/api/pay), or a host and path (api.example.com/api/pay); * is a wildcard in either

count.description: how many matching calls to wait for (default 1)

since.description: only count what arrived after this seq; without it the whole log counts, calls made before the wait included

timeout.description: give up after this many seconds (default 10, at most 300). Your own client may time out sooner, so keep a long wait within whatever it allows

q.description: name=value, repeatable: only count calls whose query carries this value

tools.name: reset
tools.description: Clear what one test case leaves for the next: script ctx.state and the replay counters, and with requests the request log as well. Neither flag means the state alone.

key.description: only this rule's state, as a rule key; without it, every rule's

state.description: clear ctx.state and the replay counters (the default)

tools.name: set_config
tools.description: The switches a whole run is set by: how an endpoint with no rule is answered, which session recording and replay use, and what the request log keeps. Only the fields passed change.

default_mode.description: how an endpoint with no rule of its own is answered: reach the server the client was calling, or answer from the recordings

session.description: which recordings this run writes and reads; one switch moves a run onto another account

max_requests_history.description: how many requests the log keeps

auto_record_requests.description: whether requests reach the log at all

allow_clients.description: addresses or CIDR ranges the proxy port accepts; empty means this machine and the private network ranges

redact_headers.description: header names whose values get_request hides

replay_marker.description: whether a replayed answer says so, with an x-tunnel-replay header

tools.name: decrypt
tools.description: Which hosts the proxy decrypts. Nothing HTTPS is read until its host is on the include list, so this comes before any rule for one. remove takes hosts off again, exclude edits the list that wins, enabled is the switch over both.

hosts.description: host or host:port entries; * is a wildcard in the host, and no port means any port

remove.description: take these off the list instead of putting them on; one that is not there is an error

exclude.description: edit the exclude list rather than include. exclude wins, and is where an SDK that pins its certificate goes so that it keeps working

enabled.description: the master switch: off decrypts nothing, however long the include list is

tools.name: record
tools.description: Keep the calls that reach the real server, to replay later. One switch over all passthrough traffic rather than a mode a rule is in: start it, stop it, or ask how it stands.

action.description: start recording, stop it, or report whether it is on and how much it has

session.description: record into this session, moving the run onto it; with start only

tools.name: list_recordings
tools.description: What has been recorded: one row per call, carrying the session and seq get_recording takes. This is what a rule in replay mode has to choose between.

session.description: only this session; without it, every one

key.description: only this rule key; wildcards allowed

host.description: only this host; * is a wildcard

tools.name: get_recording
tools.description: One recorded call in full, headers and bodies. Read one before writing a script around ctx.recorded(): this is the shape that hands back.

session.description: the session, as list_recordings reports it

seq.description: the seq, as list_recordings reports it

tools.name: check
tools.description: Send one real request through the proxy port and show what came back, verified against tunnel's own CA — the way a device's request arrives. How a rule or a script is proved before anything is told to trust it.

url.description: the full URL the client would call, scheme and all

query.description: name=value, repeatable: added to whatever query the URL already carries

data.description: a request body: JSON written out, @path to read it from a file here, or plain text

server/discover.instructions: Call the guide tool before writing rules: it returns tunnel's AGENTS.md, which covers the handler(ctx) API, how a rule key is matched and how replay chooses a recording — the things these schemas cannot say.
